summary: Forest County tower on the NHLR: 80-foot Aermotor LS-40 built 1928, registered 2017; the record's coordinates point well outside Forest County.

facts.status_note: Newest source read is the NHLR entry registered December 6, 2017; no source read confirms its condition in 2026

events.note: Register gives 1928 as the build year
Fourth annual picnic of the Tionesta Fire Tower crew held at the tower, west of Tionesta
The Tionesta towerman also spotted a column of smoke that the Titusville airport had reported
Fire set by a farmer clearing an old field; under control before any crew was sent
A big bear gave four Department of Forests and Waters employees two anxious hours near the Tionesta tower, which was being painted
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on December 6, 2017

evidence.quote: This 80-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower has been protected the northwestern corner of Forest County since 1928.

evidence.supports: Administered by the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry

sources.title: Tionesta - FOREST LOOKOUTS (quoting newspapers of 1937, 1947 and 1968)

corrections.why: The NHLR entry gives these coordinates for the Forest County tower; the record's point lies far outside Forest County. Editor to confirm before applying.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspapers of 1947 and 1968 name the State Department of Forests and Waters; the NHLR entry names the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry as administrator. Both names are reported; the NHLR name is used as the current agency.

notes_for_editor: Build year, height and registration rest on the NHLR entry; the 1937-1968 items come from newspapers quoted on the Weebly index. The standing status is inferred from the 2017 NHLR listing; no 2026 source was read, so the story does not promise a visit. Access and visit are omitted because no source describes them. The NHLR wording 'has been protected the northwestern corner' reads as 'has protected' (fire coverage), and the story paraphrases it that way. Not used: a YouTube short about a 1969 'vanished lookout' at Tionesta, because it is unreliable. Corrections entry proposes the NHLR coordinates; the brief's point is outside the county, so the editor should check before applying. Reads: 4 pages (Weebly, NHLR entry, NHLR Pennsylvania list, a Pennsylvania Wilds travel article with no tower content); 2 searches.
